findings.title: YAML-to-flat-dict key mapping is unspecified
findings.description: The YAML schema uses nested keys with different names than code/CLI (e.g., training.learning_rate vs lr, data.demo_episodes vs episodes). No flattening or renaming function is specified. merge_training_config does a simple dict update, so mismatched key names cause silent drops.
findings.fix: Add a _YAML_TO_FLAT mapping table and a _flatten_training_config(raw) -> dict helper in forge_train.py, called between load_training_config and merge_training_config.

findings.title: model.* and data.* YAML config keys have no specified code path to consumers
findings.description: model.hidden_layers/obs_dim/act_dim are validated but train_bc has no parameters for them and creates PolicyNetwork with defaults. data.target_object has no CLI flag and no extraction from merged config. The Main Flow step 6 says 'call train_bc with merged params' but doesn't show how model/data config reaches PolicyNetwork or collect_demos/from_run_dirs.
findings.fix: Option A (recommended): construct PolicyNetwork from model config in CLI and pass via network= param; pass target_object from config to collect_demos/from_run_dirs; update Main Flow steps 5-6 to show these data flows. Option B: remove model.* and data.target_object from validation and mark them as comments in YAML.

findings.title: Empty dataset guard listed in error table but not in train_bc narrative
findings.description: §10 lists 'Empty dataset -> ValueError' for train_bc but §2 does not mention adding this guard. Existing code has no such check.
findings.fix: Add 'if len(dataset) == 0: raise ValueError("Dataset is empty")' to §2 input validation block.

findings.title: code_defaults dict in merge_training_config is incompletely specified
findings.description: code_defaults is shown as {"epochs": 100, "batch_size": 64, "lr": 1e-3, ...} with a ... placeholder. The complete set of keys is ambiguous, especially for validation_split, checkpoint_interval, target_object, and model keys.
findings.fix: After resolving findings 1 and 2, list the complete CODE_DEFAULTS dict with all keys that participate in the merge.
